sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Woodbridge?
sections.html:
Woodbridge Township has no certificate of continued occupancy, but a house cannot close without a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate and a sanitary sewer discharge inspection. The sewer check is the part sellers trip over, since cemented floor drains, sump pumps and downspouts tied to the sewer all have to be dealt with first.

Woodbridge is also large and varied. With roughly 105,000 residents spread across ten communities, it covers waterfront flood zones, older Rahway Valley streets and highway-side neighborhoods, so the same inspection list affects houses very differently from one section to the next.

sections.h2: How does the Woodbridge housing market look on paper?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 103,639 people in the 2020 census and estimates 104,802 for mid-2025. Woodbridge covers 23.26 square miles of land, and about 66 percent of its homes are occupied by their owners, which leaves roughly a third of households renting.

A $433,000 median value crosses the $350,000 line in the state transfer fee schedule, so a typical Woodbridge seller pays the higher tier set. At the median price, the three bands of $2.90, $4.25 and $4.80 per $500 add up to about $3,530.

sections.h2: Which Woodbridge community is my house in, and does it matter?
sections.html:
Woodbridge Township is an umbrella for ten unincorporated communities. The Census Bureau tracks these as separate places, and the 2020 counts show their scale:

  • Iselin, 20,088 residents;
  • Woodbridge Proper, 19,839;
  • Colonia, 18,609;
  • Avenel, 16,290;
  • Fords, 12,941;
  • Port Reading, 3,921, with Keasbey, Sewaren, Hopelawn and Menlo Park Terrace making up the rest.

That matters when you sell: a mailing address may name Iselin or Colonia, but the municipality that bills the tax and requires the inspections is Woodbridge Township in every case. Woodbridge itself is the oldest original township in the state, granted a royal charter on June 1, 1669.

sections.h2: How do the Turnpike, Parkway and train stations affect Woodbridge values?
sections.html:
The township hosts the junction of the New Jersey Turnpike and the Garden State Parkway, and it is the headquarters of the agency that runs both. The Parkway runs 7.5 miles through town between Exits 127 and 132, and the Turnpike passes through for about 5.25 miles with its Exit 11. U.S. Routes 1 and 9 and Routes 27, 35, 184 and 440 add to a road network of 303.32 miles, of which 244.16 miles are municipal.

Rail runs through three stations. Metropark, on the Northeast Corridor, had 3,702 average weekday boardings in 2025, the seventh highest on NJ Transit, and Amtrak stops there as well. Avenel and Woodbridge stations are on the North Jersey Coast Line. Buses 115 and 116 go to Port Authority.

Houses within a short drive of Metropark or an Exit 127 to 132 ramp attract commuters, while houses beside the highways face traffic noise, so describe both honestly in a listing.

Woodbridge Township School District has 25 schools and 13,836 students as of 2022-23, with Colonia, John F. Kennedy Memorial and Woodbridge high schools plus the RISE program.

sections.h2: How does Woodbridge's flood risk affect selling?
sections.html:
About 19 percent of Woodbridge lies within FEMA flood hazard areas, according to Wikipedia's account of the township's floodplain studies. Water borders the township on three sides, with the Arthur Kill to the east, the Raritan River to the south and the Rahway River to the north, and some developed land sits as little as five feet above sea level.

Hurricane Sandy in October 2012 hit the Watson-Crampton area beside the Woodbridge River hard, and the township then used the state's buyout program to purchase and demolish many homes in flood hazard areas. If your house is near the Woodbridge River, Heards Brook, the Raritan in Keasbey, or the Arthur Kill in Sewaren and Port Reading, buyers and their lenders will ask about flood zone status and insurance history.

Gather your flood insurance policy, any elevation certificate and records of past claims before listing. Cash buyers care about the same things but can price the risk into an offer rather than waiting for an insurance quote.

sections.h2: What inspections does Woodbridge require for a resale?
sections.html:
The township's certificate of compliance sheet states that Woodbridge does not require a Certificate of Continued Occupancy, but that it requires a smoke detector inspection under an April 15, 1980 ordinance and a sanitary sewer discharge inspection under an ordinance adopted March 3, 1998. The form is not available online, so you schedule by phone with the buyer's name, address, email and phone number and a closing date.

  • Smoke detectors must be on every level, mounted with screws, and battery models must be the ten-year sealed type since January 1, 2019.
  • Carbon monoxide detectors must be within 10 feet of sleeping areas.
  • Open building permits and violations must be closed before the inspector releases the certificate.
  • An owner or representative must be at the house during the inspection.
  • The certificate is valid for 60 days from the inspection date.

The sewer discharge rules are where houses fail. The township's sanitary sewer page lists the prohibited connections: roof drains and downspouts, basement floor drains, sump pumps, yard and driveway drains, and missing or cracked trap caps. Floor drains must be plugged and covered with concrete, and sump pumps and downspouts must discharge to the street or yard instead of the sewer. Fix these before you call for the inspection.

sections.h2: Where is the deed recorded, and how do Woodbridge taxes work?
sections.html:
Woodbridge is in Middlesex County, so the deed goes to the County Clerk's Registry at 75 Bayard Street, 4th Floor, in New Brunswick. Hours run Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:10 p.m., and you must arrive by 4 p.m. Appointments are not required, though customers who book one are served first. A deed must carry the words "Prepared by," the tax block and lot and the sale price, and a paper recording without a cover sheet draws a $20 indexing charge.

Tax bills are mailed each January and July, and taxes are due the first day of February, May, August and November. The Tax Collection Office is in Town Hall at 1 Main Street, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday and until 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays, and payments can also go in the drop box in front of Town Hall. Sewer is billed separately, with the second half due October 1, and the township says it goes by the date it receives a payment, not the postmark.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Woodbridge?
sections.html:
A listing suits a well-kept house in a strong section, a cash offer suits one with flood, sewer or repair issues, and a sale on your own fits an owner who can run showings and the contract. In Woodbridge the sewer inspection and flood questions often tip the choice.

  • List if your sewer connections are clean and the house shows well.
  • Sell on your own if you will handle the inspections and the Middlesex County recording yourself or through an attorney.
  • Take an as-is cash offer if the house has an illegal sewer connection, past flood damage, open permits or tenants, since a buyer can absorb those costs.

Whatever you choose, schedule the township inspection as soon as the closing date is set, and compare written offers on what you net after the transfer fee, taxes and your mortgage payoff.

faqs.q: Does Woodbridge require a certificate of occupancy to sell?
faqs.a: No. The township says it does not require a Certificate of Continued Occupancy. It does require a smoke and carbon monoxide inspection and a sanitary sewer discharge inspection before a sale.

faqs.q: What is the Woodbridge sanitary sewer discharge inspection?
faqs.a: It checks that no roof drains, floor drains, sump pumps or yard drains feed the sanitary sewer and that trap caps are intact. An ordinance adopted March 3, 1998 requires it before a resale.

faqs.q: How long is the Woodbridge certificate of compliance valid?
faqs.a: Sixty days from the date of inspection. Schedule it close enough to closing that the certificate does not lapse.

faqs.q: When are Woodbridge property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Bills are mailed in January and July, and the tax collection office is in Town Hall at 1 Main Street.

faqs.q: Where is a Woodbridge deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Middlesex County Clerk's Registry, 75 Bayard Street, 4th Floor, New Brunswick. The office is open Monday to Friday, and you must arrive by 4 p.m.
